questions.question: Ava holds a solid wooden block. It has 6 flat faces in all. Two of the faces are identical rectangles that lie opposite each other and are parallel — these are its bases. The other 4 faces are rectangles that join the two bases. The block has no apex, meaning there is no single point where the side faces all come together. Is this block a prism or a pyramid, and why?
options: A prism, because it has two identical parallel bases joined by side faces and no apex.
A pyramid, because its side faces touch the bases along their edges.
A pyramid, because it has more than 5 faces.
A prism only if the 4 side faces are squares; with rectangle side faces it cannot be a prism.
questions.explain: A prism has two identical parallel bases and no apex; a pyramid has one base and one apex where all the side faces meet. Decide by counting the bases and looking for an apex — never by what the side faces look like.

questions.question: Liam has a solid plastic block shaped like a little tent. It has 5 flat faces: two identical triangles that sit opposite each other and are parallel, plus 3 rectangles that join those two triangles. There is no apex — no point where all the side faces meet. What is this solid called?
options: A rectangular prism, because 3 of its 5 faces are rectangles.
A triangular prism.
A triangular pyramid, because it has triangle faces on it.
A rectangular pyramid, because the rectangle faces rise up from the bottom.
questions.explain: Two identical parallel bases and no apex means prism, and a prism is named by its bases — the triangles. The 3 rectangles are only the side faces, so the name 'rectangular prism' is the common trap here.

questions.question: Maya sets a solid clay block on her desk. It has 5 flat faces: one square face resting on the desk, which is its base, and 4 triangle faces that all rise up and meet at a single point at the top. What is this solid called?
options: A triangular prism, because 4 of its faces are triangles.
A triangular pyramid, because its side faces are triangles.
A square pyramid.
A square prism, because its base is a square.
questions.explain: One base plus one apex where the side faces meet means pyramid, and a pyramid takes its name from its base — a square here. The trap is naming it from the 4 triangle side faces; every pyramid has triangle side faces, so they can never give the name.

questions.question: Noah gets a solid box of chocolates. Counting carefully, he finds it has 8 flat faces: two identical hexagon faces that are opposite each other and parallel, plus 6 rectangles joining them. There is no apex anywhere on the box. Which statement about the box is true?
options: It is a rectangular prism, because 6 of its 8 faces are rectangles.
It is a rectangular pyramid, because the 6 rectangles lean up from the hexagon.
It is a hexagonal pyramid, because its base is a hexagon.
It is a hexagonal prism, because its two identical parallel bases are hexagons.
questions.explain: Two identical parallel bases and no apex means prism, and the base shape gives the name, so this is a hexagonal prism. Counting the 6 rectangles and calling it 'rectangular' names it by a side face instead of a base.

questions.question: Solid A has one octagon base (8 sides) and one apex where all its other faces meet. Solid B has two identical parallel octagon bases and no apex. Which statement is true?
options: A has 9 faces and B has 10 faces.
A has 9 faces and B has 9 faces.
A has 8 faces and B has 10 faces.
A is a rectangular prism and B is a triangular prism, because of the shape of their side faces.
questions.explain: A pyramid has one side face for each edge of its base plus the base itself, so 8 + 1 = 9; a prism has one side face for each base edge plus two bases, so 8 + 2 = 10. Forgetting to count the base (or the second base) is the usual slip.

questions.question: A solid has two identical parallel bases that are rhombuses — quadrilaterals with 4 equal sides — and the 4 faces joining the bases are rectangles. There is no apex. What is the best name for this solid?
options: A rectangular prism, because all 4 of its side faces are rectangles.
A rhombic prism — a prism whose bases are rhombuses.
A rectangular pyramid, because the rectangles meet along the top edge.
A rhombus pyramid, because a rhombus is a quadrilateral.
questions.explain: With two identical parallel bases and no apex it is a prism, and the base shape names it, so rhombus bases give a rhombic prism. Calling it 'rectangular' uses a side face for the name, which is the mistake to watch for.

questions.question: Jayden's teacher describes a mystery solid: it has 6 vertices in all, and exactly one of them is an apex where 5 faces come together. What is the solid?
options: A pentagonal prism.
A triangular prism, since it also has 6 vertices.
A pentagonal pyramid.
A rectangular pyramid.
questions.explain: Only pyramids have an apex, and 5 faces meeting there means the base has 5 sides, so it is a pentagonal pyramid. A triangular prism does have 6 vertices too, but it has two bases and no apex — the vertex count alone cannot decide it.

questions.question: Sofia volunteers at a school science night, sorting model solids into a 'prism' bin and a 'pyramid' bin. Which single question about a solid will always tell her which bin it belongs in?
options: Are any of its faces rectangles?
Does it have more than 5 faces?
What shape are its side faces?
Does it have two identical parallel bases, or one base and an apex?
questions.explain: Prisms have two identical parallel bases and no apex; pyramids have one base and one apex, so that is the question that always decides. Looking at the side faces fails, because a triangular prism has rectangle sides and a square pyramid has triangle sides.

questions.question: Liam builds a solid from straws and clay: two identical parallel triangle faces joined by 3 rectangle faces, with no apex. He writes 'rectangular prism' on the label, saying that most of its faces are rectangles. What should the label say, and why?
options: It should say triangular prism, because a prism is named by its two identical parallel bases — here, the triangles.
Nothing is wrong — a solid is named after the kind of face you see most often on it, and 3 of the 5 faces are rectangles.
It should say rectangular pyramid, because the rectangle faces lean toward the top, which is what a pyramid's faces do.
It should say triangular pyramid, because it has triangles and 5 faces altogether, just like a pyramid with a square base.
questions.explain: A prism is named by its two identical parallel bases, so triangle bases make it a triangular prism no matter how many rectangles are on the sides. Counting side faces to pick the name is exactly the trap Liam fell into.

questions.question: At a campout near Squamish, Priya's tent is shaped like a solid with 2 identical parallel triangle bases and 3 rectangle side faces. Her gift box is shaped like a solid with 1 square base and 4 triangle faces that all meet at one point on top. How many faces do the two shapes have altogether, and which one is the pyramid?
options: 10 faces in all; the tent is the pyramid, because its side faces are rectangles.
10 faces in all; the gift box is the pyramid, because it has one base and an apex.
10 faces in all; both are pyramids, because both have triangle faces.
9 faces in all; the gift box is the pyramid.
questions.explain: The tent has 2 + 3 = 5 faces and the gift box has 1 + 4 = 5 faces, giving 10 in all, and only the box has one base with an apex, so only it is a pyramid. Forgetting to count a base gives 9, and having triangle faces does not make a solid a pyramid — the tent's triangles are its two bases.

questions.question: Two students describe their solids without showing them. Ethan says: my solid has 6 faces and 12 edges, and it has no apex. Kaia says: my solid has 5 faces and 8 edges, and all of its side faces meet at one apex. Both say their bases are quadrilaterals. Which pair of names is correct?
options: Both are prisms, because both have square or rectangle faces on them.
Ethan has a quadrilateral pyramid and Kaia has a quadrilateral prism.
Ethan has a quadrilateral prism (a box shape) and Kaia has a quadrilateral pyramid.
Ethan has a triangular prism and Kaia has a triangular pyramid, because of their triangle side faces.
questions.explain: No apex plus two identical parallel bases means prism, while one base plus an apex means pyramid, and the quadrilateral bases give both their names. The apex is the deciding clue — Kaia's triangle side faces belong to a pyramid but never supply its name.

questions.question: A museum in Kelowna shows 5 model solids. Their numbers of faces are 5, 5, 6, 5 and 9, so the mode of the face counts is 5. A visitor says: the mode is 5, and a solid with 5 faces is a pyramid, so most of these models are pyramids. Is the visitor right?
options: Yes — any solid with exactly 5 faces has to be a pyramid, because a pyramid is the only solid with a base and four faces rising from it, and 1 + 4 = 5.
Yes, because the mode of the face counts is 5, and 5 faces always means one base and one apex, so the mode proves that most of the models are pyramids.
No — a solid with 5 faces must be a rectangular prism, because its side faces are rectangles, and rectangles are the faces a prism is named after.
Not necessarily — a 5-faced solid can be a square pyramid (one base, one apex) or a triangular prism (two bases, no apex), so check the bases and apex.
questions.explain: The number of faces alone never settles it: a square pyramid and a triangular prism both have 5 faces, so you check whether there are two identical parallel bases or one base with an apex. Judging by face count, or by the rectangles on the sides, is what leads to the wrong name.
